Management framed 2023 as the best earnings year in company history; Celsius is now truly a billion-dollar brand at just over $1.3B revenue, up 102%.
Celsius became the first company in over a decade to break the 10-share barrier, hitting a record 11.5 MULOC share; the energy category is now a 'three-team race'.
Near-complete US distribution at 98%+ ACV; the three forward growth levers are distribution points per location, non-tracked channels, and international expansion.
Full-year gross margin expanded over 660 bps to ~48%, driven by raw material sourcing efficiency, product waste reduction, lower package costs, and promotional allowance leverage.
Q4 carries recurring seasonality vs Q3 - reduced display activity competing with seasonal items pressures both revenue and margin; not a one-time anomaly.
Robust innovation pipeline: Celsius Essentials 16-oz line (49% ACV, described as incremental, not cannibalizing), new Vibe flavors, Fizz Free non-carbonated line.
Non-tracked channels strong: Club +83.6% FY, Amazon #1 energy position at $100.1M (+72.9%), food service now 12.5%+ of PepsiCo sales.
2024 shelf-space planning was conducted in Q3 2023 at a double-digit share vs 2023 planograms set at ~4.5 share - a structural tailwind to 2024 shelf space.
Spring resets run January through May; placed >10,000 branded coolers (+300%); cold availability is the biggest opportunity ('if it's cold, it's sold').
International expansion methodical: Canada launched mid-January 2024 (exceeding expectations), UK/Ireland via Suntory beginning gradually in Q2 in the fitness channel.
Management deliberately cautious on guidance ('prudent to give ourselves additional time') citing macro uncertainty on operational and promotional fronts.
Management declined to give a forward market share target or comment on future price increases despite a competitor having taken a rate increase.
Convenience is the biggest opportunity - Celsius only at a ~10 share in convenience vs ~16 in food and ~20 on Amazon.
ROI discipline emphasized - 'John and I require an ROI on everything we do'; will invest ahead of growth where the opportunity exists, otherwise lever.
Gross margin step-down & channel inventory disconnect

Why did Q4 gross margin step back from Q3 even after adjusting for the prior-quarter promotional allowances accrual, and how to model 2024? Separately, scanner data plus disclosed Amazon/Costco sales imply a 'fairly big disconnect' to actual Q4 sell-in - did Celsius under-ship somewhere in the channel?

Management was pleased with margins (full year up >660 bps); cited the Essentials launch and Q4 innovation launches with room to improve. Q4 saw seasonal channel-inventory impact mainly in food and large format. On a net-net days-on-hand basis with the largest distributor, inventory was in good shape - innovation pipe-fill offset legacy reductions. Follow-up: as of 12/31 days on hand were consistent; January innovation rollout has been successful and incremental.

How to think about the share trajectory from here and what is the new target now that 10% is passed? Follow-up: international revenue contribution, additional 2024 markets, and why Suntory for UK/Ireland?

Declined forward share guidance; pointed to current trajectories - ~20 share on Amazon, 12 key markets ahead of 15 share, only ~10 share in convenience (the biggest opportunity), ~16 in food, all excluding the new Essentials line. Canada entered with strong acceptance; Suntory chosen for UK partly for gym-community access; methodical, build-loyal-foundation-first approach.
How quickly can unmeasured channels (corporate cafeterias, universities, vending) ramp? And should investors expect an EBITDA/EBIT margin dip in 2024 from the Canada/UK/Ireland launches?

Food service is now 12%+ of PepsiCo revenue with broad TAM; too early to size, clearer over 12-24 months. Canada and UK ramp on different trajectories - Canada benefits from an existing co-packer and US proximity, UK launches from zero. International investment will not be a significant component of growth or cost infrastructure in 2024; prepared-remarks numbers can absorb it. UK already shows higher-than-expected brand awareness.
Gross margin vs competitor pricing & Amazon drivers

With a larger competitor having taken a rate increase and sentiment another will follow, how does Celsius manage price gaps and is there margin upside? Follow-up: drivers of the better-than-expected non-measured/Amazon revenue?

Celsius positions as a premium-priced product, competitively priced per ounce, with multiple levers beyond frontline pricing (promotional strategies, pricing architecture by channel/pack size, Essentials line extension); no comments on future price increases. Amazon had a great quarter with shipment timing dynamics; Celsius is #1 energy on Amazon at ~20 share - continued growth opportunity.
Is the Q4 23% S&M rate the right full-year 2024 assumption? Follow-up: where can Essentials ACV go - can it reach 80%+ by year-end?

Q1 carries activations (Super Bowl, Jake Paul fight, MLS kickoff, F1); full-year historical range is 22%-24%, 20% YTD 2023 - use those data points; spending is ROI-driven. Essentials is the first new line launched with PepsiCo, well received and incremental (not cannibalizing); only 8-12 weeks of data - the summer resets will give a better read.
Food service step-up & new SKU incrementality
What drove the food-service step-up (from ~10% to 12.5% of PepsiCo revenue) and which channels? What incrementality do new Vibe and Core SKUs show, and what is the SKU-count limit?

Food service step-up reflects continued momentum - college program fully in place in Q4, growth across hospitals, Jersey Mike's, Dunkin'; vending also routes through food service. The 10%-to-12% move illustrates the non-tracked opportunity. Vibe will be a separate line to scale; Core team keeps producing strong flavors; Celsius does annual SKU rationalization, cutting slow-moving tail SKUs.

What is the channel strategy for placing branded coolers, and what uplift/velocity/repeat rates do branded-fridge locations show? Follow-up: are cooler SKUs consistent across the portfolio or do they vary?

Cold placement is a long-running initiative - Celsius historically sold warm, building a loyal consumer who chills it at home. Placed ~10,000 coolers, investing in more, wants placement at checkout at eye level ('if it's cold, it's sold'); substantial but hard-to-quantify uplift. Coolers follow a standard national planogram with size-based progressions, some regional seasonality, and retailer-exclusive flavors; Core, Vibe, Fizz Free and Essentials each have their own planogram.
